topics.title: Vol I: Leave, Shift Trades & Hours (103)
topics.sub: Vacation, sick and emergency sick leave, bereavement, LTD, shift trades (AWRs), industrial leave, maximum hours and L493 Days.
concepts: 103.01: Each six-month auction: bid up to 15 vacation shifts, awarded max 5 (10/year). Cancel full-shift vacation 72 hrs ahead; partial leave max 7.5 hrs.
103.02: 56-hr members call 262-SICK by 0530 (no voicemail). Doctor's proof for leave over 2 shifts (48 hrs); 6 occurrences in 12 months may bring counseling.
103.02A/B: Minor family emergency = up to 10 hrs sick leave; major = 3 shifts +1 out-of-state. Bereavement (56-hr) = 2 shifts +1 out-of-state.
103.02C/D: 30 calendar days of sick leave may trigger an HWC exam, repeated every 30 days. 40-hr staff notify Section Head by 0800; proof after 3 working days.
103.04: LTD starts 90 days after disability; all leave credits used first; ends at 80th birthday for sworn.
103.05: Max 45 AWRs per contract year, repaid within 12 months. The reliever enters it in Telestaff before 10pm the day prior and owns the shift.
103.06: Industrial leave pays net take-home up to one year per injury (2,912 hrs for 56-hr). After-hours injury: Alarm Room/on-call HWC; report to HWC next business day.
103.07/103.10: No more than 3 consecutive 24-hr shifts, then 24 hrs off; a 16+ hr partial counts as a shift. Four L493 Days a year (one per quarter), no trading.

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, in each six-month Semi-Annual Vacation Auction, how many shifts may a 56-hour member bid on and be awarded?
cards.a: Bid on up to 15 shifts and be awarded a maximum of 5.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: Each member "may bid on a maximum of fifteen (15) shifts" and be awarded a maximum of five (5). The two auctions together keep the yearly maximum at 10 awarded shifts.
opts: Bid on up to 15; awarded a maximum of 5
Bid on up to 10; awarded a maximum of 5
Bid on up to 15; awarded a maximum of 10
Bid on up to 20; awarded a maximum of 6

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, how far ahead must you contact the Time Management Coordinator to cancel a full shift of awarded vacation?
cards.a: No later than 72 hours before the shift.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: To cancel full shift vacation, the member must contact the Time Management Coordinator "no later than 72 hrs prior to the shift." After hours, weekends and holidays, call South Shift Command.
opts: No later than 72 hours before the shift
No later than 24 hours before the shift
No later than 48 hours before the shift
No later than 7 days before the shift

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, what is the most partial-shift leave you can take, and what happens if you need more?
cards.a: 7.5 hours; anything more requires taking the entire shift off, if available.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: Partial leave requests can be for a maximum of 7.5 hours; more than that "will require the employee to take an entire shift off if available."
opts: 7.5 hours; more means taking the whole shift off if available
8 hours; more needs Battalion Chief approval for the extra time
10 hours; more means taking the whole shift off if available
7.5 hours; any extra is charged as comp time automatically

cards.q: You're a rover with a partial-shift leave scheduled today. Per M.P. 103.01, when must you tell your Company Officer?
cards.a: At the start of the shift.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: Rovers "must notify their Company Officer of any partial shift leave at the start of their shift" so staffing conflicts can be planned for.
opts: At the start of your shift
At least one shift before
By 0530 on the day of leave
When you leave the station

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, you're awarded vacation shifts at auction but don't have enough vacation credits. What happens to that time?
cards.a: It defaults to Leave Without Pay unless you call Time Management in advance to change it to comp time.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: Awards are not authorization to take leave without credits; the member "will default to Leave Without Pay (LWOP)." It does NOT automatically switch to Comp Time; you must call Time Management in advance.
opts: It's LWOP unless you ask Time Management to make it comp time
It automatically draws from your comp time bank instead
The award is cancelled and goes back to the waiting list
It is borrowed against next year's vacation accrual

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, who decides whether to grant emergency vacation when a critical need for leave arises that fits no other leave type?
cards.a: SSC/ERSO.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: Emergency vacation is unscheduled vacation for a critical need; "The determination to grant emergency vacation will be made by the SSC/ERSO."
opts: SSC/ERSO
Your Battalion Chief
The Time Management Coordinator
Your Company Officer

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, Semi-Annual Vacation Sign-Up awards are based on what?
cards.a: Seniority in classification (FF, Engineer, Captain), with shifts allocated by rank and ALS/BLS classification.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: Awards are "based on length of time in classification" seniority, and shifts are allocated by rank and ALS/BLS classification in proportion to Operations staffing.
opts: Time in classification, allocated by rank and ALS/BLS
City hire date, allocated evenly across all ranks
The order bids were entered in the TeleStaff auction
Academy class rank, allocated by station and shift

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, when can a new member first use vacation credits?
cards.a: Only after six months of City employment.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: "Eligibility to use vacation credits shall begin only after six (6) months of City employment."
opts: After six months of City employment
After three months of City employment
After the 12-month probation ends
After one full year of paid service

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.01, you change shifts at your own convenience after the vacation auctions. What happens to your awarded vacation?
cards.a: You forfeit the awards and must request waitlist vacation on your new shift.
cards.why: M.P. 103.01: "Members changing shifts at their own convenience will forfeit current vacation awards and must request through waitlist vacation on their new shift." Like leave may be given only for Department-requested moves.
opts: You forfeit it and must request waitlist vacation on the new shift
It moves with you to the same dates on your new shift
ERSO grants you like leave on the new shift automatically
It is converted to comp time to use later in the year

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02, a 56-hour member too ill to work must call in no later than what time on the day sick leave begins?
cards.a: 0530 hours.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02: Notification shall be made "NO LATER THAN 0530 HOURS ON THE DAY THE SICK LEAVE IS TO BEGIN." Day-of call-ins should be made between 0430 and 0530.
opts: 0530 hours
0600 hours
0700 hours
0800 hours

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02, you call the sick line (262-SICK) and no one answers. Can you leave a voicemail?
cards.a: No. You must talk to a South Shift Command or ERSO staff member.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02: "A member calling in sick must talk to a South Shift Command or ERSO staff member, there will be No Voicemail Option."
opts: No; you must talk to South Shift Command or ERSO staff
Yes; a voicemail on the sick line counts as notice
Yes, as long as you also text your Company Officer
No; you must call your Battalion Chief directly

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02, a 56-hour member needs proof of medical treatment for sick leave lasting longer than what?
cards.a: More than 2 shifts (48 hours).
cards.why: M.P. 103.02: "Proof of medical treatment shall be required for any leave extending over (2) shifts (48 hours)" and must come from the member's own physician, not the Health Center.
opts: 2 shifts (48 hours)
1 shift (24 hours)
3 shifts (72 hours)
4 shifts (96 hours)

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02, you go home sick in the middle of a shift and then take the next two shifts off. How many sick leave occurrences is that?
cards.a: One occurrence (and it requires a doctor's slip).
cards.why: M.P. 103.02: An occurrence is sick leave over 4 hours used consecutively before returning to work. The MP's own example (home mid-shift, then two shifts off) "would be one (1) occurrence and would require a doctor slip."
opts: One occurrence
Two occurrences
Three occurrences
None; it was under 72 hours

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02, after how many sick leave occurrences in the previous 12 months may a 56-hour member be counseled and required to bring proof for future illnesses?
cards.a: Six occurrences.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02: "After (6) sick leave occurrences in the previous 12-month period, the member may be counseled" and, at the Battalion Chief's discretion, proof may be required for future illnesses.

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02, while on sick leave, which of these is allowed without prior Battalion Chief approval?
cards.a: Documented therapy treatments prescribed by a physician.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02: Members must stay home in a recuperative manner and may not do other work or recreation; seeing a physician, getting medicine and "documented therapy treatments prescribed by a physician" are allowed.
opts: Physician-prescribed, documented therapy treatments
Coaching your child's weekend league game
Working a short shift at your side job
Light workouts at the gym to speed recovery

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02, if you must provide medical treatment slips, when must you sign the sick leave documents at your Battalion Office?
cards.a: No more than 2 shifts after returning to duty.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02: Members required to provide slips must sign the documents "AT THEIR BATTALION OFFICE NO MORE THAN 2 SHIFTS AFTER THEIR RETURN TO DUTY."
opts: Within 2 shifts after you return
Before your first shift back
Within 5 shifts after you return
Within 30 days after you return

cards.q: A school calls to say your sick child must be picked up. Per M.P. 103.02A, how much emergency sick leave may you use?
cards.a: Up to 10 hours, with vacation or comp time for the rest of the time needed.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02A: A school sending a sick child home is an example of a minor emergency that qualifies for "a maximum of ten (10) hours." Vacation, comp time or unpaid leave may cover the remainder.
opts: Up to 10 hours; vacation or comp covers the rest
Up to 24 hours; the rest of the shift is covered
Up to 4 hours; the rest is unpaid leave
Up to 12 hours; vacation covers the remainder

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02A, what is the maximum major emergency sick leave for a 56-hour member?
cards.a: Three shifts plus one shift for out-of-state travel.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02A: Major emergency sick leave shall not exceed "Three (3) shifts plus one (1) shift for out-of-state travel for 56-hour members" (5 days plus 2 for 40-hour members).
opts: 3 shifts, plus 1 shift for out-of-state travel
2 shifts, plus 1 shift for out-of-state travel
5 shifts, plus 2 shifts for out-of-state travel
3 shifts, plus 2 shifts for out-of-state travel

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02A, which situation may qualify for the maximum use of emergency sick leave (a major emergency)?
cards.a: Being present for an immediate family member's major surgery.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02A: Major emergencies include being present during major surgery of an immediate family member, a family member in intensive care, or a physician requesting your presence. A normal delivery or a sick child sent home from school are 10-hour examples.
opts: Being present for a family member's major surgery
Taking a pregnant spouse in for a normal delivery
Picking up a sick child the school is sending home
Arranging home care for a family member's minor illness

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02A, which relative is included in "immediate family" for emergency sick leave?
cards.a: A stepchild.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02A: Immediate family for 103.02A is Mother, Father, Husband, Wife, Child, Stepfather, Stepmother, Stepchild, Brother or Sister. Grandparents are not on this list (they are for bereavement).
opts: A stepchild
A grandparent
A niece or nephew
A first cousin

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02B, how much bereavement leave is a 56-hour member allowed?
cards.a: Two shifts, plus one shift for out-of-state travel.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02B: "Two (2) shifts, plus one (1) shift for out-of-state travel will be allowed for 56-hour employees." 40-hour employees get 3 working days plus 2 for out-of-state travel.
opts: 2 shifts, plus 1 shift for out-of-state travel
3 shifts, plus 1 shift for out-of-state travel
2 shifts, plus 2 shifts for out-of-state travel
1 shift, plus 1 shift for out-of-state travel

cards.q: Your aunt dies, and she is not immediate family under M.P. 103.02B. What leave can you request?
cards.a: Emergency vacation through the on-duty South Shift Commander (or scheduled vacation/comp time).
cards.why: M.P. 103.02B: "For family members who are not considered immediate family, Emergency Vacation time may be requested through the On Duty South Shift Commander."
opts: Emergency vacation through the on-duty South Shift Commander
Bereavement leave approved by your Battalion Chief
Emergency sick leave through the Health Center
Unpaid general leave through Fire Personnel

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02B, which of these counts as immediate family for bereavement leave?
cards.a: Your spouse's mother.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02B: Immediate family includes "the mother and father of the employee's spouse," grandparents, grandchildren, step-siblings, a domestic partner and others listed. A spouse's siblings are not listed.
opts: Your spouse's mother
Your spouse's sister
Your spouse's grandparent
Your brother's wife

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02C, after how much sick leave may a member be required to take a medical exam by the Health and Wellness Center clinician?
cards.a: 30 calendar days.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02C: A member off on extended sick leave "(30 calendar days) may be required to submit to a medical examination by the Fire Department Health and Wellness Center Clinician."
opts: 30 calendar days
14 calendar days
60 calendar days
10 working days

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02C, while a member remains on extended sick leave, how often are additional medical exams done?
cards.a: At 30-day intervals, unless the HWC clinician directs otherwise.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02C: "Additional medical examinations shall be made at thirty (30) day intervals as long as the member is on sick leave, unless otherwise directed by the Health and Wellness Center Clinician."
opts: Every 30 days
Every 14 days
Every 60 days
Every 90 days

cards.q: You're on extended sick leave after surgery. Per M.P. 103.02C, what must happen before you return to regular or light duty?
cards.a: A medical evaluation by the HWC clinician, bringing a release from your treating physician.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02C: A member on extended sick leave due to injury or surgery "will be required to submit to a medical evaluation by the Health and Wellness Center Clinician" and must bring the treating physician's release.
opts: HWC clinician evaluation, with your doctor's release
Send your doctor's release to your Battalion Chief
Pass a fitness evaluation at the Training Academy
Have the Personnel Officer approve your release

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02D, a 40-hour staff member too sick to work must notify whom, and by when?
cards.a: Their Section Head (or designee), no later than 0800 that day.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02D: Notify "the Section Head (or designee)" as soon as it is known, "but no later than 0800 the day the sick leave is to begin."
opts: Their Section Head (or designee), by 0800
South Shift Command on the sick line, by 0530
Their Section Head (or designee), by 0730
The Health Center front desk, by 0800

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02D, a 40-hour member must provide proof of medical treatment for illnesses lasting longer than what?
cards.a: Three working days.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02D: "Proof of medical treatment is required for all illnesses extending over a period of three (3) working days" and may be requested for any illness.
opts: 3 working days
2 working days
5 working days
1 working day

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02D, after how many sick leave occurrences in the previous 12 months may a 40-hour member be counseled?
cards.a: Five occurrences.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02D: "After (5) sick leave occurrences in the previous 12 month period, the member may be counseled" and the Section Head may require proof for future illnesses. (For 56-hour members it is 6.)

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02D, when does a 40-hour member returning from sick leave sign the required sick leave documents?
cards.a: On or before 0830 the day they return to work.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02D: "On or before 0830 hours the day the member returns to work, s/he will report to the Section Head (or designee) and sign the required sick leave documents." They must sign before taking any other leave.
opts: By 0830 on the day they return
Within 2 shifts of returning
By the end of their first week back
Before 0800 on the day before return

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02E, a pregnant member who needs a Transitional Work Assignment should contact whom?
cards.a: The Fire Department Health and Wellness Center.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02E: "The member should contact the Fire Department Health and Wellness Center if they need a Transitional Work Assignment due to pregnancy," and notify their supervisor they are reporting to the HWC.
opts: The Health and Wellness Center
The Emergency Response Staffing Office
Fire Human Resources
Their Battalion Chief

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02E, how often must a member on a pregnancy Transitional Work Assignment check in at the HWC?
cards.a: Every 30 days.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02E: Once assigned, the member "may remain on transitional work for the duration of their pregnancy and check in at the HWC every 30 days."
opts: Every 30 days
Every 14 days
Every 60 days
Every 90 days

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02E, after postpartum personal leave ends, how long may the member again be eligible for a Transitional Work Assignment?
cards.a: Up to one year (longer only with Review Committee approval).
cards.why: M.P. 103.02E: After personal leave the member "will again be eligible for a Transitional Work Assignment for up to one year." Extensions beyond one year go to the Review Committee.
opts: Up to one year
Up to six months
Up to 90 days
Up to two years

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02F, the Alternate Assignment/Industrial Review Committee makes its recommendations to whom?
cards.a: The Assistant Chief of Human Resources.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02F: "Based on the review of the facts in each case, the committee will make recommendations to the Assistant Chief of Human Resources."
opts: The Assistant Chief of Human Resources
The Fire Chief
The Local 493 President
The Deputy Chief of the Health Center

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.02F, how often does the Alternate Assignment/Industrial Review Committee meet?
cards.a: Monthly or as needed.
cards.why: M.P. 103.02F: The committee "will meet monthly or as needed, as determined by the Assistant Chief or Deputy Chief of Personnel."
opts: Monthly or as needed
Quarterly or as needed
Weekly
Twice a year

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.04, when does long-term disability eligibility begin?
cards.a: Ninety days after the disability commenced.
cards.why: M.P. 103.04: Eligibility: "Ninety (90) days after disability commenced."
opts: 90 days after the disability began
30 days after the disability began
60 days after the disability began
180 days after the disability began

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.04, what must happen to your sick leave, vacation, and comp time before you're eligible for long-term disability?
cards.a: All accumulated leave credits must be used first.
cards.why: M.P. 103.04: The MP notes that "all accumulated leave credits must be used prior to eligibility for long-term disability (sick leave, vacation, compensatory time, personal leave, etc.)."
opts: They must all be used up first
They are paid out at 50 percent
They are frozen until you return
They are converted into LTD credit

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.04, long-term disability benefits end for a sworn member at what birthday?
cards.a: The 80th birthday.
cards.why: M.P. 103.04: Benefit termination includes the "Eightieth (80) birthday for sworn members" (75th for civilian members).
opts: 80th
75th
65th
70th

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.04, a member with a pre-existing condition becomes eligible for LTD benefits after what total waiting period?
cards.a: 24 months (an additional 12 months beyond the first 12).
cards.why: M.P. 103.04: An applicant with a pre-existing condition "will be eligible for LTD benefits when an additional 12-month period (total 24 month waiting period) is met."
opts: 24 months
12 months
18 months
36 months

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.05, what is the maximum number of shift exchanges (AWRs) per employee in a contract year?
cards.a: Forty-five.
cards.why: M.P. 103.05: "Members may be granted the opportunity to exchange shifts up to a maximum of forty-five (45) per employee in a contract year."

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.05, within what time frame must AWRs be repaid?
cards.a: Within 12 months.
cards.why: M.P. 103.05: "It is the employee's responsibility to insure all AWRs are repaid within a 12-month time frame."
opts: Within 12 months
Within 6 months
Within 90 days
Within 24 months

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.05, who is responsible for the Telestaff AWR entry, and by when?
cards.a: The member providing relief, before 10pm the day before the AWR.
cards.why: M.P. 103.05: "It is the responsibility of the employee providing relief" to ensure the Telestaff entry is completed "prior to 10pm the day prior to the AWR occurring."
opts: The member providing relief, before 10pm the day prior
The member requesting relief, before 10pm the day prior
The member providing relief, before 0700 the same day
The Battalion Chief, at the start of the AWR shift

cards.q: You enter an AWR in Telestaff at 2300 the night before the shift. Per M.P. 103.05, what must you do?
cards.a: Contact SSC staff between 0500 and 0600 that day about the late entry; approval is at their discretion.
cards.why: M.P. 103.05: Late entries after 10pm "must communicate with SSC staff between 0500 and 0600 hours on the day of the shift." Approval is at the discretion of the on-duty South Shift Commander or SSC staff.
opts: Call SSC staff between 0500 and 0600 that day
Email ERSO before midnight to get it approved
Call your Battalion Chief before 0700 for approval
Nothing more; the late entry auto-approves

cards.q: You entered an AWR to work another member's shift but now can't make it. Per M.P. 103.05, who must find coverage?
cards.a: You, the member who agreed to work it.
cards.why: M.P. 103.05: Once the reliever completes the Telestaff entry, "FULL RESPONSIBILITY FOR THAT SHIFT" is theirs; if they can't work it, "it is his or her responsibility to find someone qualified to work it."
opts: You, the member who agreed to work it
The member who originally asked for relief
South Shift Command through constant staffing
Your Battalion Chief, using an available rover

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.05, what is the penalty for failing to provide relief on an AWR you agreed to work?
cards.a: Loss of vacation time equal to the cost of filling the position, and possible loss of AWR privileges.
cards.why: M.P. 103.05: "FAILURE TO PROVIDE RELIEF WILL RESULT IN A LOSS OF VACATION TIME EQUAL TO THE COST OF FILLING THAT POSITION, AND MAY RESULT IN THE LOSS OF THE EMPLOYEE'S AWR PRIVILEGE."
opts: Vacation time equal to the cost of filling the spot
Two shifts of comp time are taken from your bank
A written reprimand on the first offense
Repaying the shift at time-and-a-half

cards.q: You need a 3-hour partial shift trade. Per M.P. 103.05, what is required?
cards.a: Prior supervisor approval; no Telestaff entry is required under 4 hours.
cards.why: M.P. 103.05: "No Telestaff entry is required for less than four (4) hours, however, any relief time must have prior supervisor's approval." Partials of 4 hours or more follow the full AWR procedure.
opts: Prior supervisor approval; no Telestaff entry needed
A full Telestaff entry before 10pm the day prior
Nothing; trades under 4 hours need no approval
Battalion Chief approval plus a Telestaff entry

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.06, how long can a 56-hour member on industrial leave stay on payroll at net take-home pay?
cards.a: Up to one year per injury (2,912 hours for 56-hour members).
cards.why: M.P. 103.06: Members are paid up to their regular net take-home pay "for up to one year total per injury." Leave beyond one year per injury (2,912 hours for 56-hour; 2,080 for 40-hour) is not paid leave.
opts: Up to one year (2,912 hours) per injury
Up to six months (1,456 hours) per injury
Up to one year (2,080 hours) per injury
Up to two years (5,824 hours) per injury

cards.q: It's 2200 and you have a minor on-duty injury you feel should take you off duty for the rest of the shift. Per M.P. 103.06, what do you do?
cards.a: Contact the after-hours on-call HWC clinician through the Alarm Room.
cards.why: M.P. 103.06: For a minor after-hours injury, "the after-hours on call Health and Wellness Center clinician may be contacted through the Alarm Room." If this step is skipped, the member is charged their own time.
opts: Reach the on-call HWC clinician through the Alarm Room
Call your Battalion Chief for approval to go home
Go home and report to the HWC within 72 hours
Call South Shift Command to send you a relief

cards.q: You're treated in an emergency room for an after-hours industrial injury. Per M.P. 103.06, when must you report to the HWC?
cards.a: On the next business day.
cards.why: M.P. 103.06: "The member must report to the Health and Wellness Center on the next business day for evaluation" to continue or change their off-duty work status.
opts: The next business day
Within 72 hours
At the start of your next shift
Within 5 working days

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.06, which on-duty injuries must be reported to the Alarm Room?
cards.a: All injuries requiring any level of treatment.
cards.why: M.P. 103.06: "THE ALARM ROOM SHALL BE NOTIFIED OF ALL INJURIES REQUIRING ANY LEVEL OF TREATMENT SO THAT PROPER NOTIFICATIONS CAN BE MADE."
opts: All injuries requiring any level of treatment
Only injuries that need hospital transport
Only injuries that happen after business hours
Only injuries that cause lost time from duty

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.06, a member on industrial leave needs Industrial Commission of Arizona permission to travel out of state for more than how many days?
cards.a: 14 days.
cards.why: M.P. 103.06: "Members who are on Industrial Leave and need to travel out of state for more than 14 days require permission from the Industrial Commission of Arizona."
opts: 14 days
7 days
30 days
3 days

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.06, which industrial injuries require an additional Third-Party Agreement form?
cards.a: Injuries from a motor vehicle accident, animal bite, or assault.
cards.why: M.P. 103.06: "If the injury is sustained due to a motor vehicle accident, animal bite or assault, an additional form: the Third-Party Agreement" shall also be completed.
opts: Vehicle accidents, animal bites, and assaults
Burns, falls, and smoke inhalation injuries
Exposures, needle sticks, and lifting strains
Any injury that results in lost time

cards.q: You've just worked three consecutive 24-hour shifts. Per M.P. 103.07, what's the rule now?
cards.a: You must be off duty a full 24 hours before working again.
cards.why: M.P. 103.07: Members shall not work more than three consecutive 24-hour shifts; "members must be off-duty a full 24 hours before working again."
opts: Be off a full 24 hours before working again
Be off a full 12 hours before working again
You may work a fourth if it's constant staffing
Be off a full 48 hours before working again

cards.q: Per M.P. 103.07, a partial shift of how many hours or more counts as a full 24-hour shift toward the maximum hours rule?
cards.a: 16 hours or more.
cards.why: M.P. 103.07: "If a member is called to work a partial of any kind greater than or equal to 16 hours, the shift will be considered a full 24-hour shift."

12 hours
8 hours
20 hours

cards.why: M.P. 103.07: "Working both an AM and PM overtime opportunity on the same day will also be considered a 24-hour shift."

As two separate partial shifts

topics.title: Vol I: Overtime, Assignments & Staffing (104)
topics.sub: Overtime and court standby, transfers and assignments, staff and specialty positions, transitional work, seniority, constant staffing and the Emergency Reserve Program.
concepts: 104.01: Overtime must be authorized by your supervisor before you work it; submit at the end of that workweek. Two 24-hr comp slots per shift.
104.01A: Court standby pays $1.50/hr, self-cancels at 1700; request due to Pay and Benefits within 5 calendar days.
104.02: Transfer ads open at least 12 days; occupy within 30 days and stay 6 months. Absent 12 straight months (or 12 in 18) = assignment revoked.
104.02: Max 200 shifts on a rescue; rovers call SSC 0615-0645; out-of-class rovers commit to 90 days.
104.02B: HWC assigns transitional work up to 3 months (+3 by HWC head); beyond 6 months goes to the TW Review Committee. Contact HWC within 1 business day of release.
104.02E/G: FIT offered in rank order on the BC promotional list, not seniority. C957 vacancies filled from back-ups by seniority in rank.
104.03: Sign up for constant staffing before 0500; answer within 10 minutes; a refusal = 1.5 opportunities. Fill order: rovers, promo lists, out-of-class, constant staff.
104.03B: Everyone gets 2 Emergency Reserve days per quarter; be available 0800-1100; leave doesn't excuse it; one like-for-like trade per quarter.

Payroll, when the form is entered

At the end of the calendar month
